summary: Re-enables outgoing email (password resets, invitations, notifications) by relaying Postfix through PostShiba with SMTP auth (hatchbox/main.cf, root-deploy installs a credentials file), removes the 'email deliverability problems' banners from the forgot-password and invite forms, and updates the About page; root-deploy has a filename typo (installs sasl_password but postmaps sasl_passwd) that breaks the deploy script/email (fixed later in 12ca89f).

statements.why: root-deploy:67-68 installs $APP_ETC/sasl_password but runs `postmap /etc/postfix/sasl_passwd` under `set -e`, so the deploy script aborts before `postfix reload` and main.cf's smtp_sasl_password_maps points at a missing map; email stays broken (upstream 12ca89f 'fix typo... presumably the reason for recent email failures'). Also needs an SMTP secret file on the server.
True, but doesn't say it now names PostShiba as the email host.
True; it removed the 'email deliverability problems' warning banner, which the card doesn't say.
True, but doesn't say all site email now relays through PostShiba (smtp.postshiba.com:587 with SASL auth) or the postscreen_blacklist_action -> denylist rename.
True, but presented as a plain file change: it installs libsasl2-modules and an SMTP credentials file, and contains the sasl_password/sasl_passwd typo that breaks the deploy.

misses.what: Server deploy script typo: copies sasl_password but postmaps /etc/postfix/sasl_passwd; with set -e the root deploy fails and outgoing mail (password resets, invites) stays broken in production.

All outgoing email now relays through a third-party provider (PostShiba) using SMTP credentials that must be placed on the server ($APP_ETC/sasl_password) before deploy; the card lists the hatchbox files but says nothing about the new secret or vendor.
Warning banners about email problems are removed from the password-reset and invite pages, so users are no longer told email might fail (bad if the fix doesn't work).
Postfix config change: postscreen_blacklist_action renamed to postscreen_denylist_action (requires a Postfix version that supports the new name).
